text:
SRE Bot: ALERT -> redis-cluster-prod: high_command_latency fired (severity=P1). Flooding PD. See: https://alerts.redwood.prod/alert/1795551234 :rotating_light:
Emma: noticed a huge spike in `redis_cmd_latency_seconds` at ~16:03 UTC, looks correlated with a big ML batch write job. Paging started. :eyes:
Raj: I'm primary oncall, jumping in. Are we seeing user impact or just background jobs?
Olivia: Quick check — dashboard shows 30% of requests hitting >500ms for caching tier, errors are still low but tail latency causing downstream timeouts for search. Customers might see slow search.
Mike: Confirming PD notifications are duplicating across multiple alerts (one per instance). It's basically 12 pages for the same incident. :face_with_head_bandage:
Emma: For immediate mitigation we should: 1) mute instance-level alerts, 2) enable grouping in Alertmanager (group_by=cluster, severity), 3) add a rate_limit window so PD isn't flooded. Can implement temporary change now.
Raj: +1. Make the temp change and then we can plan durable tuning post-incident. Who can flip the Alertmanager config?
Olivia: I can push a temporary patch to alertmanager-routing: set `group_by: ['cluster','alertname']` and `repeat_interval: 30m` for this alert. Also add `rate_limit` at 5/min for alertmanager -> PD.
Emma: If you push that, also create an inhibition rule so instance-level `HighLatency` is inhibited if `ClusterHighLatency` is firing, otherwise we'll still get duplicates. Example inhibition:
```yaml
inhibit_rules:
  - source_match:
      alertname: "ClusterHighLatency"
    target_match_re:
      alertname: "InstanceHighLatency.*"
    equal: ["cluster"]
```
Raj: Good, that avoids losing signal but stops the noise. Olivia, please go ahead and ping when it's live.
Olivia: Pushed to staging and then to prod. Alertmanager reloads succeeded. Changing grouping & inhibition now.
SRE Bot: CONFIG -> Alertmanager reload OK (v2.3.1). rate_limit set to 5/min for route `high-latency`.
Mike: PD is quieting down. I still see a couple of duplicates but much better. Thanks. :thumbsup:
Emma: We should also create a short-lived dashboard that surfaces the affinity of this alert to K8s jobs (job labels) — helps root cause and avoid future false positives. I'll sketch one: panels for per-job tail-latency, job throughput, and per-instance p95.
Lucy: For the post-incident follow-up: 1) refine alert thresholds to use rolling p95 vs instant, 2) add alert fingerprinting in Alertmanager using `fingerprint_templates` to dedupe variants, 3) add runbook steps to check for batch jobs before paging. I'll open a ticket with owners.
Raj: Assign steps: Olivia - temp alertmanager changes (done), Mike - update PD escalation policy to use grouped incidents, Emma - create dashboard draft, Lucy - ticket + runbook. Target: docs + PRs by EOD tomorrow.
Olivia: Opening PRs: alertmanager config change (temp) and a follow-up PR with suggested stable config (grouping + rate limiting + inhibition). Link in thread: https://git.redwood/ops/alerting/pulls/542
Mike: Also recommend we add a short suppression window for alerts triggered by job-controller cronjobs (label `job_type=maintenance`) — maybe `for: 10m` so transient spikes don't page.
Emma: Agreed. For long term: evaluate moving instance-level alerts to low-severity (warning) unless they persist for >5m or correlate with cluster-level signals.
Lucy: I'll include all of these in the post-incident checklist. Quick customer impact note for ops: no confirmed data loss, increased latency for a subset of search queries for ~22 minutes, mitigated by routing and alert config changes.
Raj: Thanks team. I'll follow up with a short incident summary for CS so they can proactively message affected customers. Marking this thread as actioned. :white_check_mark:
